Definition: feminine of πρυμνύς (hindmost); the stern of a ship:--hinder part, stern.
BiblicalUsage: Prymna is the stern, the hinder part of a ship. Jesus was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow, when the storm arose. On Paul's voyage, the sailors cast four anchors out of the stern and wished for the day, and the ship ran aground, the forepart stuck fast, and the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the stern is where men look when they are afraid: the disciples woke Jesus there, and the sailors anchored from there, because the back of the ship is where you brace for what is coming.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
